PILLAR 01

Executive Calendar & Scheduling

A zero-conflict, color-coded schedule across time zones, with focus time protected and buffers built in. Tools: Calendly, Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook.

PROBLEM REDUCED

Double-bookings, missed time-zone conversions and back-to-back meetings with no recovery time. Every invite is cross-checked across 4 time zones, protected by buffers before and after calls, and held to a 24-hour minimum notice, so each executive day stays clear and prepared.

15 / 30 minbuffers before / after calls

Calendly booking rules
  • Availability 13:00–20:00 EAT, overlapping Europe and North America
  • 15-minute buffer before calls, 30 minutes after strategy meetings
  • 24-hour minimum notice to prevent last-minute collisions
  • Calendly connected to Google Calendar
Time zone conflict rules
  • Cross-check every invite in EAT (UTC+3), UTC, EST (UTC-5), PST (UTC-8)
  • Re-check daylight saving offsets before quarterly recurring meetings
Every invite includes
  • Direct Zoom or Google Meet link
  • Agenda link or bulleted objectives
  • Required vs. optional attendees

PILLAR 04

Executive Technical & Systems Support

Step-by-step SOPs for common problems, so fixes are repeatable and documented.

PROBLEM REDUCED

Slow, undocumented fixes that come back. Each sample ticket follows a Problem, Diagnosis, Resolution path with a stated response time. First responses land within 8 to 12 minutes, 18 stuck client records were replayed with zero data loss, 340+ SKUs were normalized in 20 minutes, and access for 8 contractors was restored in 15 minutes.

8-12 minfirst-response SLAs
0data loss on replay
95%faster client onboarding
15 minescalation rule
Access control issues (locked out, wrong permissions)
  • Confirm who is affected, which system, and the exact error message
  • Verify identity through the approved channel before changing anything
  • Reset the password or MFA, or adjust access using least privilege
  • Test the login with the user, then log the ticket: cause, fix, time taken
System patches and updates
  • Check release notes and schedule outside meeting hours (see calendar rules)
  • Back up or note the current version, then notify the executive
  • Apply the update and restart if needed
  • Verify key apps still work, record the version in the log
Basic service outage
  • Check the provider status page and test from a second device or network
  • Restart the app, router or session; clear the cache if relevant
  • If unresolved in 15 minutes, escalate to the provider or IT with a clear summary
  • Send a status update, then a closing note with root cause

Technical Incident Triage Runbook (4 steps)
  1. Acknowledge: confirm the alert, log the ticket and reply within 15 minutes
  2. Classify: set priority (P1 to P3) from impact, number of users and affected systems
  3. Diagnose: run health checks, review logs and recent patches or changes, in both on-premises and cloud systems
  4. Resolve and document: fix, roll back or escalate to Tier-2, then update the ticket and knowledge base with the cause and prevention steps

CASE STUDY

E-Commerce Fulfillment & Dispatch System in Airtable

An order, pick and dispatch system for a small coffee and cold-pressed juice business, built from a raw CSV into a live operations dashboard. sample dataset

PROBLEM REDUCED

Orders buried in raw rows, cold-chain breaches nobody sees and dispatches nobody logs. The system turns 50 orders into focused views, flags 13 cold-chain orders (12 breaches and 1 warning) automatically, splits the pick list into groups of 15, 13 and 15, and logs every dispatch with no manual entry.

50orders organized
13cold-chain orders flagged
15 / 13 / 15orders per pick group
0manual log entries

Click a card to reveal its screenshot proof.

Data Organization & Cleaning

I imported the raw CSV, highland_husk_bean_dispatch_starter.csv, and rebuilt it as a relational base: an Orders table linked to a ProductsCatalog and a Fulfillment Log. Each of the 50 orders has an Order ID, SKU, quantity, order and production dates and a category. Typed fields replaced loose text, so orders can be filtered, grouped and counted reliably.

Three product categories

Every order belongs to one of three categories: Whole Bean, Cold-Pressed Juice or Ground. The dashboard chart shows the category breakdown (total count: 50) so stakeholders see it without opening a single row.

Custom Views & Filtering

The Cold-Chain Alert view isolates temperature-sensitive juice orders, flagged by formula: 13 orders, 12 breaches and 1 warning.

Morning Pick List

Filtered by fulfillment status and grouped by category: Whole Bean (15), Cold-Pressed Juice (13), Ground (15). Together with the Grid view of all orders, that makes three views and no manual sorting.

Workflow Automation

The rule "When Fulfillment Status is Dispatched, create a record in Fulfillment Log" handles the repetitive logging, keeping a live audit trail with no manual entry.

Executive Interface & Dashboard

Built in Airtable Interface Designer, with live cards for Ready to Ship (21), Awaiting Production (8), In Production (14), Overdue Orders (43) and Cold Chain Breach (12).

PROJECT

Automated Revenue Operations Pipeline

From a won deal to a sent invoice and a Slack alert, with no manual steps. Below: how the tools connect in a live setup, then a simulator you can run.

PROBLEM REDUCED

Copy-pasting between a CRM, a payment tool, accounting software and chat: slow, and easy to get wrong. The pipeline connects 4 tools in 4 stages with 0 manual steps, uses 1 idempotency key per deal so a retry can never double-bill, and sends failures to a dedicated Slack channel in the same run.

4tools connected
0manual steps (simulated)
1idempotency key per deal

Real-World Implementation Blueprint

1

Airtable CRM

The trigger source. When a deal in the Deals table moves to Closed Won, an automation fires with the deal, amount and owner.

Trigger
2

Zapier

Receives the webhook, authenticates to Stripe and QuickBooks through OAuth, and uses Formatter to clean amounts and dates.

Orchestration
3

Stripe + QuickBooks

Stripe creates and sends the invoice. QuickBooks records the matching invoice so the books stay in sync.

Invoicing
4

Slack

Posts the invoice summary to #revenue-ops. Failures go to #ops-errors so nothing is missed.

Alerts
What makes it production-ready
  • Idempotency key per deal, so a retry never creates a second invoice
  • OAuth connections with token refresh handled by Zapier
  • Formatter step to convert amounts to cents and dates to ISO 8601, preventing 400 schema errors
  • Error path: failed steps alert Slack and can be replayed from Zap history
  • Write-back: invoice ID and status return to Airtable, keeping one source of truth

Data Backup, Version Control & Hygiene Log

The protocol I use for catalog and inventory files, drawn from my Shopify and Airtable work.

  • Daily: export the CSV from Shopify or Airtable and save it before any edits
  • Naming: YYYY-MM-DD_Inventory_Master_v2.csv, never overwrite, always bump the version
  • Backup: keep at least two copies, one in secure cloud storage
  • Duplicates: match on SKU, keep the latest row, and log every removed row
